question: Does adding more public Perturb-seq screens raise the 55% trustworthy coverage?
verdict: NO. All available large Perturb-seq screens target the same K562-expressed / essential-gene space the genome-wide screen already covers, so the union adds only ~19 genes (55%->55%). The only screen that could add many new genes (Joung 2023 TF atlas, ~1,700 TFs) is OVEREXPRESSION -- a different modality from the knockdown debugger -- and 5.8GB (download throttled). The deeper barrier: the ~7,800 unmeasured genes are largely NOT EXPRESSED in K562, so no K562 screen reaches them, and no public genome-scale KNOCKOUT Perturb-seq exists in a complementary cell type. The 55% ceiling is DATA-GENERATION-limited (needs new wet-lab screens in other cell types), not fetch-limited.
